summary: Qu states that Qu Pay brings payments into the same restaurant platform, with one agreement, one support path, and unified reporting and reconciliation. Qu claims brands can go live in days and reduce onboarding timelines by up to 75%. Treat the timing and 75% figure as Qu-reported vendor claims.
source: Qu, “Restaurant Payments, AI, and What's Next for Operators,” LinkedIn, 2026-09-10 — https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/restaurant-payments-ai-whats-next-operators-qupos-fqh4e/

summary: Qu identifies Golden Chick as a customer with more than 250 restaurants across six states. Qu reports that order-confirmation boards and outside line-busting tablets drove a 30% improvement in order accuracy systemwide; third-party integration timelines improved 4x from weeks to days; 24/7 hypercare supported pilot launches; Qu serves as the restaurant-platform foundation for standardized expansion; and Voice AI pilots are underway. The case study provides no measurement period, baseline, sample size, rollout coverage, or independent validation, so all results remain vendor-reported.

Qu’s 2026 State of Digital & Beyond research says it surveyed 168 QSR and fast-casual brands representing more than 94,000 locations. Qu reports 73% are investing in AI now or within one year; among brands already pursuing AI, 43% report limited value, 33% emerging value, and 9% meaningful or transformational impact. Qu’s stated takeaway is to define the business outcome, build on connected data, forecast consumption and cost together, and monitor whether value grows at the same rate as consumption. Treat as vendor-sponsored research pending independent corroboration.
source: Qu, “Restaurant Payments, AI, and What's Next for Operators,” 2026-09-10, linking Qu 2026 State of Digital & Beyond Report — https://stateofdigital.qubeyond.com/
